correctness.rationale: For each target, killed matrices A,B of the two lazy Metropolis kernels satisfy a=1+Ab, b=1+Ba, equivalently (I-AB)a=1+A1. Connectedness and self-loops >=1/2 ensure absorption and invertibility. Frozen witness C4/paw has rational phase hitting vector (5538,3876,4236)/607 and static vectors (8,6,6) and (15,6,9); start 1 target 3 yields (3876/607)/6=646/607. The complete finite census enumerates every connected labeled graph n=2,3,4 (1,4,38), each unordered pair, all starts, targets and two phases: 4,120,17784 tests, best ratios 1,1,646/607; 168 four-state strict slowdowns and 24 extremal phase cases. I independently reimplemented exact rational killed-matrix elimination and reran this entire finite census. This is exhaustive for n<=4 and does not assert any n>4 case.
residual_risks: Result is confined to n=2,3,4, strict period-two switching, exact lazy Metropolis weights and same start/target pair. No larger-state upper bound or nonperiodic schedule claim.

value.rationale: A natural minimal-counterexample classification for two connected lazy reversible graph walks with identical stationary measure. Even though each fixed walk is well behaved, switching strictly worsens same-pair hitting, and four vertices are proved minimal with an exact 6.43-percent sharp inflation ratio. The complete finite enumeration and explicit witness are independent useful sharp facts, not an arbitrary slice of an unrelated statistic.
residual_risks: Small quantitative gain and finite dimension; significance is the first possible graph order and complete sharp counterexample, not general asymptotics.

limitations: Result is confined to n=2,3,4, strict period-two switching, exact lazy Metropolis weights and same start/target pair. No larger-state upper bound or nonperiodic schedule claim.
